criteria.title: The policy prohibits discrimination, including on grounds relevant to Indigenous identity

checks.label: A clear ban on discrimination in hiring or employment
A general equal-opportunity statement, e.g. 'equal opportunity employer'
Names Indigenous Peoples (Indigenous, First Nations, Inuit, Métis), or at least two of: ancestry, place of origin, ethnic origin, colour, creed

levels.2: A clear ban on discrimination that names grounds relevant to Indigenous identity
levels.1: A ban in general terms only, e.g. 'equal opportunity employer'
levels.0: No ban; welcoming or diversity language alone

criteria.addressedLooksLike: The policy explicitly prohibits discrimination in hiring, recruitment, and employment under the Ontario Human Rights Code AND (explicitly names Indigenous Peoples (Indigenous, First Nations, Inuit, Métis) OR lists at least two of: ancestry, place of origin, ethnic origin, colour, creed)
criteria.whyItMatters: Banning discrimination in employment is a legal duty under the Ontario Human Rights Code. It also answers the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s Call to Action 92, which asks Canadian companies to adopt UNDRIP as a framework( eg. Article 2 affirms Indigenous Peoples’ right to be free from discrimination) and to ensure equitable access to jobs. While Call to Action 92 isn’t legally mandated at this time,  aligning with it now and actioning on UNDRIP's framework puts a company ahead of the expectation.

criteria.title: Indigenous-specific hiring follows Ontario Human Rights Commission guidance
criteria.appliesWhen: The policy restricts hiring to, designates roles for, or prefers Indigenous candidates. 'Encouraged to apply' alone does not count.

checks.label: Cites a legal basis: a special program under section 14 of the Ontario Human Rights Code, or OHRC guidance
States the purpose: the disadvantage or under-representation the program addresses
Self-identification is voluntary and asked only for the designated roles
Identity is not confirmed by the employer alone with a single document (e.g. confirmation with or through Indigenous communities or organizations)

levels.2: A special program with a stated legal basis and purpose, voluntary self-identification and identity confirmation not left to the employer alone
levels.1: Some of the legal basis or purpose is stated, but the program is incomplete
levels.0: Indigenous-specific hiring with no legal basis or purpose

redFlags.label: Asks about Indigenous identity on general application forms
The employer alone confirms identity with a single document

criteria.addressedLooksLike:
The document Legal basis: names section 14 of the Ontario Human Rights Code, or section 24 with a reason.
- Purpose: says who the program helps and why.
- Eligibility: says who can apply, in a way that matches the purpose.
- Time and review: gives an end date or review schedule.
- Identity confirmation: a process that involves Indigenous people or organizations and offers more than one way to confirm.
- Data safeguards: limits on access, use only for the program, and a destruction timeline.
criteria.whyItMatters: The Ontario Human Rights Code allows Indigenous-specific hiring, but only with a proper legal basis, usually a section 14 special program, which protects the program from discrimination claims. Confirming identity carefully guards roles that genuinely rely on Indigenous identity or lived experience against inaccurate or false claims. Done well, it puts Call to Action 92’s call for equitable access to jobs into practice. The OHRC issued this guidance because many employers asked how to hire for these roles while meeting their obligations under the Code.

criteria.title: Retention and advancement supports exist

levels.1: Mentioned, but not a formal program sponsored by leadership
Mentioned, with no resources behind it
levels.2: A resourced Indigenous employee network, or sponsorship and leadership development for Indigenous employees
Formal, resourced supports including Indigenous-specific support
levels.1: Some supports exist, informally or without Indigenous-specific resources

criteria.addressedLooksLike:
The policy describes a formal mentorship program sponsored by leadership, and supports Indigenous employees’ participation in leadership and career development, such as through sponsorship or a resourced Indigenous employee network.

Promotions are decided on objective, skills-based criteria, and the process and criteria for promotions and pay increases are documented and transparent.
criteria.whyItMatters: These policies introduce structured support, advocacy, and transparent advancement  opportunities. Leadership-sponsored mentorship and a resourced Indigenous employee network can help reduce workplace isolation and connect Indigenous employees with advocates who can open doors to leadership roles. Basing promotions and pay increases on documented, objective, skills-based criteria removes subjective gatekeeping and builds trust that career growth is fair and achievable.
